validated_issues.original_description: Uses 'system' with 'rm -rf' for cleanup. While safe here with hardcoded paths, it's less portable than using Scheme-native file deletion if available.
validated_issues.reasoning: Confirmed at line 142. The use of 'system' for shell commands reduces portability, though it is common in test scripts. Low severity is appropriate.

validated_issues.original_description: map-collection throws an error if a block is missing, while fold-collection and filter-collection silently skip them. This inconsistency could lead to unexpected crashes in distributed environments.
validated_issues.reasoning: Confirmed. map-collection (line 69) uses (error ...), while filter-collection (line 82) and fold-collection (line 93) skip missing blocks. This inconsistency can lead to brittle error handling logic.

validated_issues.original_description: collection-group-by has O(N^2) complexity due to nested map/assoc usage for each element. For large collections, this will be significantly slow.
validated_issues.reasoning: Confirmed at line 184. The nested loop structure with 'map' and 'assoc' leads to O(N*G) where G is number of groups, effectively O(N^2) in worst cases.

validated_issues.original_description: collection-add and collection-merge do not check for duplicate hashes, which might lead to unexpected growth if called repeatedly with the same members.
validated_issues.reasoning: Confirmed at lines 220 and 243. No deduplication logic is present, allowing the same block hash to be added multiple times.

validated_issues.original_description: (cdr (assq 'body post)) will crash if a post is missing the 'body' field (assq returns #f). This occurs in multiple functions: find-tagged, list-all-tags, tag-histogram, etc.
validated_issues.reasoning: Confirmed as a systemic risk. While core/query/query.ss has been partially patched with 'safe-get-body' (line 32), the identical unsafe pattern '(cdr (assq 'body post))' still exists in forum/tools.ss:179 (format-post), which is called by query.ss:204. Any post missing 'body' will still crash the display logic.

validated_issues.original_description: count-occurrences is O(N^2) because it calls remove-assq inside a loop over the input list. Scalability issue for high tag counts.
validated_issues.reasoning: Confirmed at line 103. 'remove-assq' is O(N) and called for every element in the list, resulting in O(N^2) complexity.

validated_issues.original_description: Functions like find-tagged and tag-histogram call collect-all-posts on every invocation. In a large forum, this causes massive I/O overhead without caching.
validated_issues.reasoning: Confirmed. find-tagged (line 46), list-all-tags (line 76), and tag-histogram (line 99) all call 'collect-all-posts' which performs full filesystem traversal.

gaps_found.description: Inconsistent behavior for missing blocks: 'collection-all?' returns #f (failure) if a block is missing, whereas 'collection-any?' (via 'collection-find') skips missing blocks and continues searching. This leads to asymmetric logic.
'count-string-occurrences' shares the exact same O(N^2) complexity issue as 'count-occurrences' (using 'remove-assoc' in a loop), which was missed by the QA report.
The 'unique' utility function used for tag keys and values is O(N^2) due to the use of 'member' inside a loop. For large sets of tags, this adds unnecessary overhead.
Convenience functions (find-by-tag, tags, tag-report) implicitly depend on a global '(fs)' procedure being available in the environment, which may not be true in all execution contexts.

summary.notes: Most issues were confirmed, though some line numbers in the original report were slightly offset. The high-severity crash in query.ss was partially addressed by a helper function in that file, but remains a critical vulnerability in the shared 'format-post' utility. Performance gaps (O(N^2) patterns) are prevalent in the query system.
